seo.title: WordPress Analytics Without Cookies, A Google Analytics Alternative
seo.description: Add privacy-first analytics to your WordPress site without cookie consent banners. OpenPanel is cookieless, open source, has a WordPress plugin, and starts at $2.50/month: a better alternative to GA4 for WordPress.

hero.heading: WordPress analytics without the cookie banner
hero.subheading: Google Analytics on WordPress means cookie consent popups, GDPR complexity and visitor data on US servers. OpenPanel is a cookieless analytics platform with a WordPress plugin: pageviews, events and user behaviour, hosted in the EU, with no privacy headaches.

problem.title: Why Google Analytics on WordPress creates problems
problem.intro: WordPress powers 40% of the web, but GA4 was not designed with WordPress privacy requirements in mind.

items.title: Google Analytics requires cookie consent on WordPress
items.description: Installing GA4 on a WordPress site means a consent popup for every visitor. Under GDPR, you can't set GA4 cookies without explicit opt-in. That banner costs you conversions and corrupts your data.

items.title: GA4 sends data to US servers
items.description: Google Analytics transfers visitor data to US servers. For European sites, this creates legal exposure under Schrems II, a risk WordPress site owners increasingly can't ignore.

items.title: WordPress analytics plugins are bloated
items.description: Most GA4 WordPress plugins add significant weight to your site. Page speed suffers, Core Web Vitals drop, and you are still dealing with cookies.

items.title: You can't see user behavior, only pageviews
items.description: GA4 tells you how many people visited. OpenPanel tells you what they did: which CTAs they clicked, where they dropped off, which blog posts convert to signups.

features.title: Privacy-first analytics for WordPress
features.intro: OpenPanel gives WordPress site owners complete visibility without the cookie compliance headaches.

items.title: Official WordPress plugin
items.description: Install the OpenPanel WordPress plugin, paste your client id, and page view tracking starts. The plugin also proxies the script and the events through your own domain, so ad blockers do not drop them.

items.title: Automatic page view tracking
items.description: Every page, post and custom post type is tracked automatically, along with outgoing links. No configuration for standard pageview analytics.

items.title: Cookie-free by default
items.description: No cookies, no localStorage, no raw IP on events. GDPR, CCPA and ePrivacy without a banner or any configuration.

items.title: Custom event tracking
items.description: Track clicks, form submissions and conversions with one JavaScript call, or add data-track attributes to buttons and links with no code. Know which CTAs and forms bring leads.

items.title: UTM campaign tracking
items.description: See which emails, ads and social posts bring traffic to your site, and which ones convert, with source, medium, campaign, term and content on every session.

items.title: Lightweight script, about 3 KB
items.description: The tracker is a fraction of the size of GA4 and loads async. No impact on Core Web Vitals or PageSpeed scores.

items.title: Self-hostable on your own server
items.description: Run OpenPanel on your own server with Docker Compose and one install script. Your visitor data never leaves your infrastructure.

benefits.intro: OpenPanel replaces Google Analytics without sacrificing features, and fixes the privacy problems GA4 created.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions from WordPress site owners evaluating OpenPanel.

items.question: How do I install OpenPanel on WordPress?
items.answer: Install the OpenPanel plugin from the WordPress plugin directory, activate it and paste your client id. Page views track immediately. If you prefer, add the script tag to your theme's header.php or any header scripts plugin instead.

items.question: Do I need a cookie consent banner with OpenPanel?
items.answer: No. OpenPanel sets no cookies and stores no raw IP, so cookie consent does not apply. Under GDPR, consent is required when you use cookies or similar storage; OpenPanel does not.

items.question: Is there an OpenPanel WordPress plugin?
items.answer: Yes. Search for "OpenPanel" in Plugins, Add New, install it and paste your client id. The plugin loads the tracker and proxies it through your own domain. You can also add the script tag manually.

items.question: How does OpenPanel compare to MonsterInsights or Analytify?
items.answer: Those plugins are wrappers around Google Analytics: they still send data to Google and still need cookies. OpenPanel is an independent platform that is cookieless by default and stores data in Germany.

items.question: Can I track WooCommerce events?
items.answer: Yes. Hook into WooCommerce's actions (woocommerce_thankyou, add to cart) to send events, and send the order total as a revenue event from the thank-you page or your backend. No dedicated WooCommerce plugin required.

items.question: Does OpenPanel affect WordPress site speed?
items.answer: The tracker is about 3 KB gzipped and loads async; GA4 with a wrapper plugin is many times larger. Switching from GA4 will likely improve your Core Web Vitals.
